official.deadline_note: Applicants must complete the online application before 15 March; the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office must send its recommended-applicant list to the TaiwanICDF no later than 31 March, and applicants must separately meet each partner university's own admissions deadline, which can fall earlier.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 intake - 2027 application round (applications open 1 December 2026 and close 15 March 2027)
official.status_note: The official programme page states: 'The 2027 TaiwanICDF Scholarship applications open from December 1, 2026 to March 15, 2027!' - the round has not yet opened as of the verification date. Results are announced, in principle, no later than 10 June each year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The TaiwanICDF will cover the tuition fee as required by the student's university.
benefits: The total scholarship, including airfare (round-trip), housing, tuition, credit fees, insurance, textbook costs and a monthly allowance will be provided by the TaiwanICDF to each student within his/her given award period.

Bachelor's Program: Each student shall receive NT$15,000 per month during the period of the program as allowance for food and miscellaneous living expenses; the sum will be deposited monthly into the student's local bank account.

Master's Program: Each student shall receive NT$18,000 per month during the period of the program as allowance for food and miscellaneous living expenses; the sum will be deposited monthly into the student's local bank account.

Ph.D. Program: Each student shall receive NT$20,000 per month during the period of the program as allowance for food and miscellaneous living expenses; the sum will be deposited monthly into the student's local bank account.
Airfare: The TaiwanICDF shall arrange your most-direct flights to and from Taiwan with Economy Class tickets.

Housing: All students must reside in the student dormitories. Insurance fees will be covered for the entire duration of the program (mandatory student safety insurance set by the Ministry of Education plus accidental and necessary medical coverage).
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country on the List of Countries Eligible for TaiwanICDF Scholarship, and satisfy any specific criteria established by his or her country and/or government of citizenship.
Neither be a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan) nor an overseas compatriot student; applicants from non-beneficiary countries are not eligible to apply.
Satisfy the admission requirements of the partner university to which he or she has applied to study under a TaiwanICDF scholarship.

Be able to satisfy all requirements for a Resident Visa (Code: FS) set by the Bureau of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and an Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) set by the Ministry of the Interior; the TaiwanICDF has the right to revoke a scholarship offered if visa requirements cannot be satisfied.

Upon accepting a TaiwanICDF scholarship, not hold any other ROC (Taiwan) government-sponsored scholarship (such as the Taiwan Scholarship) in the same academic year; have never had any scholarship revoked by any ROC government agency or related institution, nor been expelled from any Taiwanese university.

Applicants who have already held a TaiwanICDF scholarship, MOFA's Taiwan Scholarship or an MOE scholarship must have graduated before July 31, 2025 (2026-round rule) and must provide the highest-level diploma before July 31, 2026; bachelor's programs are exclusively available to applicants from countries that maintain diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
requirements: Applicants must complete an online application in the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System (application dates: December 1, 2026 - March 15, 2027); applicants must ensure that they submit accurate and complete information, and failure to do so will result in the application not being processed.
Each applicant can only apply for one program at a time, and the applicant also needs to submit a separate program application to his/her chosen university/program.

Applicants should submit all documents required by the TaiwanICDF partner schools before the admissions deadline of that university, and submit all required documents to the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office in their home countries if necessary.
The TaiwanICDF Scholarship only offers admission for the fall semester; deferring the scholarship award is not allowed and the duration of the scholarship may not be extended.
documents: Completed TaiwanICDF scholarship online application (TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System).
The separate admission documents required by the chosen TaiwanICDF partner university, submitted before that university's admissions deadline.

Any documents required by the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office in the applicant's home country - whether hard or soft copies are required depends on the decision of each individual office.
Highest-level diploma/degree certificate, which must be provided before July 31 of the application year (July 31, 2026 for the 2026 round).
Signed consent form, read over and returned to the TaiwanICDF through the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Representative Office upon acceptance (Step 6).
selection_criteria: First review by the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative office based on the eligibility requirements and selection criteria of the TaiwanICDF; the office sends its list of recommended applicants to the TaiwanICDF no later than March 31 each year.

Second review of qualified applicants by an academic committee organized by the individual partner university in joint cooperation with TaiwanICDF representatives, based on each university's selection criteria whilst also accounting for the eligibility requirements and selection criteria of the TaiwanICDF.

Comprehensive evaluation: 'We will evaluate all applicants comprehensively, rather than accept or reject them based on one single quality. All positive features will be valued and taken into careful consideration.' (2026 Guidebook FAQ Q9)
coverage: Tuition fee as required by the student's university, and credit fees which vary with the number of credits registered.
Round-trip airfare: most-direct flights to and from Taiwan in Economy Class, arranged by the TaiwanICDF.
Housing: residence in the student dormitory is mandatory for all students.
Insurance fees for the entire duration of the program: the mandatory student safety insurance set by the Ministry of Education plus accidental and necessary medical coverage.
Textbook costs for textbooks as required by the instructors, subject to the approval of the director of the student's institute.
Monthly allowance for food and miscellaneous living expenses (NT$15,000 bachelor's / NT$18,000 master's / NT$20,000 Ph.D.), deposited monthly into the student's local bank account.
application_method: Step 1: Complete the online application in the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System between 1 December 2026 and 15 March 2027 (one program at a time).
Step 1 (parallel): Submit a separate program application and admission documents to the chosen partner university before its admissions deadline.
Step 2: Contact the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Office and submit the required documents there (hard or soft copies as the individual office decides).

Step 3-5: The office conducts the first review and forwards its recommended list to the TaiwanICDF; a joint university/TaiwanICDF committee conducts the second review; results are announced in principle no later than 10 June.
Step 6: Successful applicants return a signed consent form to the TaiwanICDF through the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Representative Office to accept the terms and become official recipients.
official.application_route: Apply online through the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System, apply separately to the chosen TICA partner university, and file documents through the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office in the home country.
official.study_mode: Full-time higher-education programs at TICA partner universities; the E-Learning Master Program of Education and School Leadership (National Chung Cheng University) is conducted online, requiring recipients to be in Taiwan only for the first-semester orientation and the fourth-semester thesis oral defense.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of countries on the TaiwanICDF's List of Countries Eligible for the scholarship and satisfy any specific criteria set by their country/government of citizenship; ROC (Taiwan) nationals and overseas compatriot students are excluded, and applicants from non-beneficiary countries are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is exclusively for students from partner/other developing countries; local (Taiwanese) students are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must route their application through the ROC (Taiwan) Embassy/Consulate General/Representative Office in their home country, may apply to only one of the offered TICA partner-university programs per year, and cannot change program after submission or after award.
official.description: The TaiwanICDF describes its International Higher Education Scholarship Program as offering full scholarships to outstanding students from partner countries to pursue higher education in Taiwan through collaborations with local universities, supporting the socio-economic growth of partner countries through the cultivation of highly talented individuals. Programs are run under the Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA) framework established with partner universities since 1998; in 2026 there are 32 programs offered for application across undergraduate, graduate and Ph.D. levels, all conducted in English.
official.program_type: International Higher Education Scholarship Program under the Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA) framework, funded by Taiwan's international cooperation and development fund
official.english_requirement: The TaiwanICDF has no requirements regarding English proficiency test; however, applicants must follow the policies of their school and program, which may include academic or language requirements such as an English proficiency test.

applicant_utility.summary: This is Taiwan's development-aid scholarship for students from listed partner countries: it covers tuition, dormitory housing, round-trip economy airfare, insurance, textbooks and a monthly living allowance of NT$15,000 (bachelor's), NT$18,000 (master's) or NT$20,000 (Ph.D.) at one of roughly 32 English-taught TICA partner-university programs. The 2027 round opens on 1 December 2026 and closes on 15 March 2027, decided through a two-stage review run by the ROC (Taiwan) embassy in your country and the partner university. You file one application in the TaiwanICDF online system, apply separately to your chosen university, and route documents through your home country's ROC (Taiwan) office; university admission alone does not mean you hold the scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants from a country on TaiwanICDF's eligible list - especially a diplomatic ally if aiming for a bachelor's degree - who want fully funded, English-taught graduate study in fields such as agriculture, public health, engineering/ICT, business, tourism or education and can commit to studying in Taiwan for the full award period.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the current List of Countries Eligible for TaiwanICDF Scholarship, and contact your local ROC (Taiwan) embassy/office early to learn whether it wants hard or soft copies and by what internal date.

Choose exactly one program from the annual 'Programs Available for Application' list and open that programme's own admission page, since its document list and deadlines are separate from and often earlier than TaiwanICDF's.
Build the calendar backwards from 15 March: online application, university admission submission, and embassy document delivery all need to be finished by mid-March.
Make sure your highest-level diploma will be awarded before the July 31 cut-off of the application year; if it will not, plan for the following year's round.
Check your chosen programme's own language and academic requirements, since TaiwanICDF imposes no English test of its own but the university may.
Keep your passport, Resident Visa (FS) and ARC planning realistic for post-award processing, and hold off on any other Taiwan-government scholarship application for the same academic year.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to more than one program: only one program per applicant per year is processed, and program changes after submission or after award are not possible.
Assuming university admission equals funding: only applicants who receive an acceptance letter issued by the TaiwanICDF are scholarship recipients.
Incomplete or inaccurate online applications: the TaiwanICDF states such applications will not be processed.
Missing the partner university's separate admissions deadline, which can be earlier than the scholarship deadline.
Skipping the embassy step or its document requirements, which breaks the first-review route that nominates you to the TaiwanICDF.

Holding or accepting another ROC (Taiwan) government scholarship (e.g. the Taiwan Scholarship) in the same academic year, or being a previous holder who has not graduated before the published cut-off.
Applying to a bachelor's program from a country without diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Personal spending beyond the monthly allowance, visa/ARC and medical exam fees, travel to the embassy or test centres, airline extras such as excess baggage, any university application fees if the chosen programme charges them, textbook purchases not approved by the institute director, and any study beyond the award period - the TaiwanICDF states additional duration of study must be taken at your own expense.
document_audit: Diploma timing trap: the highest-level diploma must be obtained before July 31 of the application year (July 31, 2026 for the 2026 round), or the applicant must wait for the next round.
Embassy offices decide individually whether hard or soft copies are required, and they set their own document flow - confirm before the March rush.
The university application is genuinely separate with its own deadline and document list; missing it ends the scholarship route.
No recommendation letters are required by the TaiwanICDF, but the chosen programme may still ask for them - check the programme page rather than assuming.
Textbook costs are only covered when required by instructors and approved by the institute director, so unapproved purchases stay out of pocket.

Book purchases, dormitory residence and insurance enrolment all assume you are physically in Taiwan from the fall semester; only the designated E-Learning program waives this except for orientation and thesis defense.
alerts: The 2027 round does not open until 1 December 2026 - early submissions are not accepted, so prepare everything in advance.
Results are announced in principle no later than 10 June, with the acceptance letter delivered via the embassy; a signed consent form must go back through the embassy to confirm the award.
There is no spring intake and no deferral - the award starts in the fall semester.
Only one program may be chosen and it cannot be changed after submission or after award; switching TICA programs cancels the scholarship.
Bachelor's places are restricted to applicants from countries with diplomatic relations with Taiwan, so non-ally applicants should target master's or Ph.D. programs.
Previous holders of a TaiwanICDF, MOFA Taiwan Scholarship or MOE scholarship must have graduated before the published cut-off (July 31, 2025 for the 2026 round) before reapplying.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online application in the TaiwanICDF system by 15 March, separate university admission submission in parallel, embassy first review and nomination by 31 March, joint university/TaiwanICDF second review, TaiwanICDF announcement by 10 June, then signed consent form returned via the embassy.
